result.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
result.summary: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Told only the symptom, an editor, a frontier multimodal LLM acting as an agent, locates the cause, edits the weights and tests them, with a failure census and instruments showing it the failing images and where the VLM attends; among several editors, the harness keeps only edits that clearly reduce the failure without lowering accuracy on questions no editor saw. The repair needs no training, keeps the model's size and per-token cost, and applies to already-edited weights. The editors expose where the loops live: from the original weights, independent editors on both models trace them to the attention outputs of the middle layers, and the smaller VLM stops consulting the image inside a loop. On Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-2B, across six image benchmarks from visual mathematics to GUI grounding, the edit removes most loops on every benchmark and shortens answers, and the edited models are significantly more accurate than the thinking models on average; the larger one gains most on GUI grounding, a task absent from the practice questions. Because the repair lives in the weights, it combines with budget forcing where held-out questions favor it: on the best available weights, Keel has the best average accuracy on both models, significantly above every training-free baseline we compare on the larger one.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Keel，一种面向图像任务的 agentic 权重编辑方法：由前沿多模态 LLM 充当编辑代理，仅凭「thinking 模式下反复自重复直到 token 上限」这一症状，借助失败普查与注意力可视化定位病灶并直接改动 VLM 权重，且只保留不损害留出题准确率的编辑，无需训练、不改变模型规模与单 token 成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益与代价问题：编辑代理把循环归因于中间层注意力输出，并观察到较小模型在循环中不再查阅图像，可供核查「视觉旁路/注意力坍缩」假设；但它是权重层面的失败修复而非 latent 推理状态生成，与长度泛化、停止决策的机制联系需读原文确认。
